report:
Reviewed the complete external_fact_queries claim, both ordinary implementation associations (external_syms.rs and TcxDb in tcx/mod.rs), and the complete sole associated test, sage_meta::todo::symbols_external_fact_queries. The requirements are owned imports, definition-keyed retrieval, no provider resolution of Sage-local names, and no provider execution of Sage trait proof or normalization; imported Sage values are the semantic boundary.

external_trait_signature, external_adt_signature, external_fn_signature, external_impl_signature, and external_trait_items pass the requested external crate number and definition index to distinct metadata methods. external_associated_type_value supplies both impl and associated-definition identities. Candidate queries remain anchored to a trait or ADT definition, with optional rigid-head/name refinement; this is external metadata filtering, not Sage-local name resolution. Sized/fundamental facts also use definition IDs. TcxDb returns owned Raw* structures containing owned vectors, strings, boxes, and value identities, without compiler or database-borrowed types. Its signatures expose neither a Sage-local resolver nor a Sage proof/normalization operation. External-crate discovery and proc-macro expansion are separate capabilities, not proof or local name-resolution callbacks.

The lowering helpers consume these owned structures and create Sage SymExt/GenericParam identities, Stash-owned types, binders, predicates, signatures, and associated projections. lower_ty preserves associated projections as Sage AliasTy values rather than requesting provider normalization; lower_predicate imports obligations rather than asking the provider to discharge them. Completeness and availability are retained as None, incomplete candidate sets, or SolverEligibility::Unsupported. Associated-value lowering obtains its binder from the separately definition-keyed impl signature. This does not promise per-fact update invalidation or forbid the required owner signature read; the distinct keyed_reuse TODO visibly records that limitation. The added TcxDb association ensures the essential provider interface participates in future review invalidation.

Test adequacy is explicitly deferred, not asserted. The only associated test has no runtime assertions and is correctly in the todo module: its comment calls for complete definition-keyed signature/body/proof/normalization traces, including rejection of unrelated metadata reads. Completing instrumented end-to-end provider request traces for these operations and asserting the permitted/requested identities and absence of unrelated requests is prerequisite to replacing this TODO. Existing unassociated helper tests in external_syms.rs are not counted as coverage of this claim. This accepted test debt means source inspection supports the boundary but does not demonstrate an executed complete behavioral matrix. No N/A or implementation-TODO entry is being relabeled as implemented.

Executed cargo meta review start, recorded dependency reads, and cargo fmt after the single association comment edit. Reviewed fresh inputs after that edit. A failed read of the nonexistent tcx.rs path was corrected to tcx/mod.rs, now included directly as implementation context. No behavioral tests were executed by this reviewer; the coordinator owns suite execution and delegated quality/sanity checks. No behavioral bug was identified, no regression reproduction is claimed, and no further edits are requested.
